_comment: Override with --config <file>. A supplied file is merged over these defaults,
so a config that only changes owner_rules keeps the scoring weights.
WHY SCORING IS CONFIGURABLE: a severity label alone is not a priority. The same
'HIGH' matters very differently on an internet-facing production IAM role than on
a logging setting in a sandbox. These weights make that judgement explicit and
reviewable instead of leaving it in an engineer's head.

category_weights._comment: Categories where a defect most directly leads to cross-tenant access or credential compromise are weighted up. Logging is weighted down slightly: a missing log is serious but it is a detection gap, not an access path.

tag_modifiers._comment: Applied multiplicatively. 'compensating_control' is the only reducer, and it requires the control to be named in the finding description.

resource_criticality._comment: First matching regular expression wins. Patterns are matched case-insensitively against the resource string.

rules.reason: IAM resources govern every other permission in the account.
On the authentication or authorization path.
Protects every other secret or encrypted object.

_comment: Score to priority band. P0 is 'stop what you are doing'; P4 is 'record it and move on'.
Calibrated so that severity alone does not reach P0: a critical finding on an
uncategorised resource scores 100 and lands in P1. Reaching P0 requires severity
AND context -- an authorization defect on an internet-facing production resource
holding customer data, for example. This is deliberate: if a quarter of the queue
is P0 then P0 means nothing and the on-call learns to ignore it.

sla_days._comment: Target days from first_observed to resolution, per priority. Used to compute an overdue flag in the report.

owner_rules._comment: First matching rule wins. A rule matches when every key it specifies matches. 'resource_pattern' is a case-insensitive regular expression.

severity_aliases._comment: Tool-specific severity labels mapped onto the normalized scale. Unknown labels become 'medium' and are counted in the report's normalization warnings, so an unmapped label is visible rather than silently downgraded.
